name: Zimelidine
summary: Zimelidine, formerly sold under the brand name Zelmid among others, is an antidepressant medication of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class, and the first SSRI antidepressant to be marketed. It is a pyridylallylamine, and is structurally different from other antidepressants.

pharmacology.text: Zimelidine acts primarily by selectively inhibiting the neuronal reuptake of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT), thereby increasing serotonin concentrations in the synaptic cleft and enhancing serotonergic neurotransmission.

uses.text: Zimelidine, formerly sold under the brand name Zelmid among others, is an antidepressant medication of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class, and the first SSRI antidepressant to be marketed. Zimelidine was first sold in 1982.

sideEffects.text: Zimelidine was generally reported to cause fewer anticholinergic, sedative, and cardiovascular adverse effects than the tricyclic antidepressants with which it was compared. Reported adverse effects included headache, nausea, insomnia, muscle pain, joint pain, fever, neurological symptoms, and abnormalities of liver function.
